title: Nobody touched the pipeline, and every build fails
role: You maintain the self-hosted GitLab runners that build every team's Docker images.

source.label: GitLab: update on Docker-in-Docker with Docker 19.03 (31 July 2019)

brief: Late July 2019. Since this morning every `docker build` job on your runners fails within seconds. The `.gitlab-ci.yml` files haven't changed in weeks. Developers are pinging you one by one in chat.

steps.situation: The job log ends the same way in every project.
steps.evidence:
$ docker build -t registry.example.com/shop/api:$CI_COMMIT_SHORT_SHA .
docker: Cannot connect to the Docker daemon at tcp://docker:2375.
Is the docker daemon running?.
ERROR: Job failed: exit code 1

choices.text: Compare the last green job with the first red one: images, versions, runner
choices.why: If your code didn't change, something underneath did. The `docker:dind` service image is untagged, so it now pulls a new major version.
Running jobs are killed, and the next job pulls the same new image and fails the same way.

choices.text: Retry the failed jobs a few times
choices.why: The failure is the same every time, so retries only fill the queue and the chat.

steps.situation: The `docker:dind` service log in a failed job shows what changed.
steps.evidence:
Using docker image docker:dind (Docker 19.03.0)
... Generating TLS certificates in /certs
... API listen on [::]:2376
... API listen on /var/run/docker.sock

choices.text: Read it: 19.03 dind now makes TLS certificates and listens with TLS, not on plain 2375
choices.why: From 19.03 the image turns TLS on by default. Your jobs still talk plain TCP to port 2375, where nothing listens.

choices.text: Blame the network team: port 2375 is being blocked
choices.why: The service and the job share a network, and the log says the daemon moved. Read the evidence before opening a ticket against another team.

choices.text: Set privileged = false to see if it helps
choices.why: DinD needs privileged mode. You'd add a second failure on top of the first.

steps.situation: Forty teams are blocked. You want builds green now, then the proper fix.

choices.text: Pin the previous dind version in a shared CI template, tell the teams, then plan the TLS change
choices.why: Pinning puts back the image that worked, a quick change you can undo. GitLab itself advises pinning a version instead of an untagged `docker:dind`.

choices.text: Set DOCKER_TLS_CERTDIR to an empty string everywhere
choices.why: GitLab lists it as a valid fix when you can't change the runner's volumes. It gets builds going, but the daemon is back on plain TCP.

choices.text: Mount the host's docker.sock into every job instead
choices.why: Builds pass, but any job can now control the host's Docker, which is root on the runner. That's a security change nobody agreed to.

steps.situation: Builds are green on the pinned version. Now do the TLS fix and stop this class of surprise.
steps.evidence:
# config.toml on the runner
[runners.docker]
  privileged = true
  volumes = ["/certs/client", "/cache"]

# .gitlab-ci.yml
variables:
  DOCKER_TLS_CERTDIR: "/certs"

choices.text: Roll out the /certs/client volume and DOCKER_TLS_CERTDIR=/certs, keep versions pinned, upgrade on purpose
choices.why: That's GitLab's TLS setup: the dind service writes client certificates to the shared volume and the job uses them. Pinned images change when you decide, through a tested merge request.

choices.text: Go back to untagged images once things work
choices.why: Then the next major release breaks every pipeline on someone else's schedule, just like today.

choices.text: Move builds to a laptop runner until it's sorted
choices.why: A single unmanaged machine becomes your release path, with secrets on it.

debrief.what_happened: Docker 19.03 changed the `docker:dind` image to generate TLS certificates and require them. GitLab jobs that used the untagged `docker:dind` service image started failing with *Cannot connect to the Docker daemon at tcp://docker:2375*. On 31 July 2019 GitLab published two fixes: configure TLS by setting `DOCKER_TLS_CERTDIR: "/certs"` and adding a `/certs/client` volume in the runner's `config.toml`, or turn TLS off with `DOCKER_TLS_CERTDIR: ""`. GitLab.com shared runners were already set up for this. GitLab also recommended pinning image versions such as `docker:19.03.0-dind` so that a new release doesn't break jobs without warning.
lessons: When unchanged code fails, compare image versions first.
Pin CI images and service images; upgrade them through a merge request.
Read the service container's log, not just the job's error line.
A quick rollback first, then the proper fix, with a note to every team.
